items.summary: A failed or malformed GitHub checkpoint must be acknowledged in the immediate correction, not silently replaced
items.details: After publishing any gate checkpoint, read back the durable GitHub comment and verify that it contains the complete signed evidence. If publication is empty, malformed, points at a temporary file, or otherwise wrong, preserve and link the bad artifact; state exactly what failed; publish the canonical replacement; and explicitly connect the two in the immediate follow-up. Transparency is part of the evidence contract: an observable correction lets the team learn, while a silent replacement hides the process failure even when the final technical verdict is correct. Use gh --body-file for file-backed comments rather than passing @path as literal --body text.
